title: Nomination vs inheritance - why a nominee isn't always the legal owner
p1:
Your nominee gets the money after you are gone. But does that mean they own it?

Many people assume the person named as a nominee automatically becomes the final owner of their assets. That assumption can create unexpected disputes.
p2:
A nominee is usually someone chosen to receive and manage an asset temporarily, making the transfer process smoother. But inheritance rules can decide who actually has the legal right to own that asset.

The surprising part: the person who receives the money first may still have to pass it on to the rightful heirs.
p3:
For example, a nominee on a bank account or investment may help the family access funds quickly, but ownership can depend on succession laws, a valid will, and other legal factors.

The practical lesson: naming a nominee is helpful, but it is not always a substitute for proper estate planning. Review your nominations and create a clear plan for your assets.
conclusion: Did you know that a nominee and a legal heir can be different people? Have you ever checked whether your nominations match your inheritance plans?
